safetyNote: Listed as edible by DGfM and Swiss VAPKO, but uncommon and locally red-listed. Eat only after reliable identification and suitable cooking. Check the pine association and a freshly cut specimen: orange latex that turns wine-red after several minutes, with strong green staining of cap, gills or stem. Similar orange milkcaps overlap in appearance; if the latex was not seen from the moment of cutting, do not rely on its later red colour alone. Seek expert review when uncertain.

sections.title: Small zoned cap that greens
sections.text: The cap is commonly 3–9 cm across, first convex with an inrolled edge and later flat to depressed. Its initially dull orange, grey-orange or grey-pink surface has weak to evident concentric zones and is slightly sticky when damp. Green to grey-green patches can form early and may come to dominate older specimens. A lilac cast may be visible before greening obscures it.

sections.title: Gills, stem and timed latex
sections.text: Close pale orange to salmon gills are attached to shortly decurrent and can green on handling. The short, pale orange-pink stem may carry scattered shallow pits and becomes hollow with age; it too can green strongly. Flesh is pale centrally, orange nearer the surface. Fresh cuts release rather scant bright orange latex; over several minutes it turns dark wine-red, while cut flesh may also become vinaceous. The spore deposit is ochre to pale ochre in published descriptions.

sections.title: Pines and similar species
sections.text: Lactarius semisanguifluus forms mycorrhizae with pines, often on calcareous soil and sometimes in grassy woodland edges. The directly blood-red latex of L. sanguifluus contrasts with its initial orange milk; the bright orange L. deliciosus usually shows less wine-red flesh and less extensive green tones. L. deterrimus is chiefly a spruce associate and also has delayed red latex, making the host and stem characters important. Exact colour-change times vary across field guides and specimens.

sections.title: Edibility and conservation
sections.text: The DGfM includes this species on its edible list but marks it Red List category 3 in Germany; the Czech Mycological Society labels it vulnerable in the Czech Republic. VAPKO also lists it. These are regional conservation assessments, not a universal collecting rule. A complete specimen and a timed fresh cut are needed for identification, while a drawing cannot demonstrate either the host association or the latex reaction.

traits: Dull orange to grey-pink cap, generally 3–9 cm, depressed with age and often strongly green-blotched
Weak to evident concentric zones, slightly viscid when wet
Close pale orange to salmon gills, attached to shortly decurrent, greening on handling
Short pale orange-pink stem, sometimes shallowly pitted, hollowing with age and often greening
Initially orange latex that turns wine-red after several minutes; pale central flesh and ochre spore deposit
European pine associate, often on calcareous soil; uncommon in some regions
